blockers.evidence: Official LocalSubprocessRuntime ordinary spawn does not need terminal inspection; spawnTerminal does. Web defaults to standard without PTY, but minimal is a shipped user-selectable preset and mounts persistent PTY. The exposed terminalInspector property is explicitly a test hook, so Android will not promote it as a production compatibility seam.
blockers.nextProbe: First prove node-pty build/load with scripts/android-native-addon-probe.sh; then add a production Android SubprocessRuntime provider or wait for upstream Android PTY support.

blockers.evidence: Official attachment-local depends on sharp. The frozen runtime lock already records sharp@0.35.4 plus exact @img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.4 and @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3; sharp's loader has a generic WASM fallback after platform-native resolution. Remaining gaps are optional-byte materialization and a real Android carrier image smoke.

The built-in sandbox-local platform chain has no Android entry, but official @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox exposes a public provider seam. Android wires a first-party Community provider through the official dsh --patch layer. It maps official writableRoots(policy) to frozen @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run@0.1.1, requires full enforcement, and preserves exit-125/signature classification. The embedded Node bootstrap is additionally wired to repeat full allow/deny confinement under the APK app UID before official DSH spawn. NDK build and real APK execution remain unproven.
blockers.nextProbe: Build scripts/android-sandbox-landlock-probe.sh, integrate the verified Node carrier, then capture android-app-uid-preflight.cjs PASS under the real APK UID.

blockers.evidence: Official alpha.4 tool-fs-search owns glob/grep semantics and resolveRgPath(). The audited search-core.ts has resolveRgPath() with zero parameters, no rgPath/ripgrepPath config/environment seam, direct Node-mode import('@vscode/ripgrep').rgPath, and a sidecar path gated only by 'pkg' in process. @vscode/ripgrep@1.18.0 has no Android platform package in the frozen lock.
blockers.nextProbe: Run scripts/audit-android-ripgrep-seam.mjs against the exact official search-core.ts during each DSH upgrade. Reopen only if a real Android @vscode/ripgrep package appears or official tool-fs-search exposes an explicit executable-path seam; do not fork/copy official glob/grep solely to replace binary resolution.

conclusion: Node 22 is necessary but insufficient. The published top-level @deepseek-ai/dsh package eagerly carries the native closure, so profile-only row disabling cannot make the current official CLI package Android-safe.
